sources.quote: The number of ED visits for e-bikes has increased nearly 10-fold from 2017 to 2023
sources.searcher_note: CPSC staff report (Sept 2024, day not printed). E-bikes only: narrative subset of code 3215 with mopeds excluded; 34,200 ED visits in 2023; 2018-2021 e-bike years below reporting threshold.

sources.quote: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission says e-bike emergency department visits nationwide increased nearly tenfold over five years, climbing to an estimated 34,200 in 2023.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff local TV coverage repeating the CPSC e-bike-only figure; also cites JAMA Surgery 751 (2017) to 23,493 (2022).

sources.quote: But prior to 2024, e-bike injuries were mixed together with moped injuries.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff analyst note on NEISS; says e-bike and e-scooter ER visits are rising, 855,000 micromobility ER visits 2020-2025; flags the pre-2024 moped mixing that the lead's code 3215 series carries.

sources.outlet: Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health
sources.quote: The rate of e-bike and powered scooter injuries surged between 2019 and 2022—by 293 percent and 88 percent, respectively
sources.searcher_note: NEISS 2019-2022 study release; e-bike injury rate (per total ED injuries) up 293%, window ends a year before the lead's.

sources.quote: Nearly half (46%) of all estimated e-bike injuries from 2017 to 2022 occurred in 2022 alone.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest CPSC release found on the e-bike surge; date as read by WebFetch though the URL path says 2024.

sources.quote: Injury patterns and safety implications for electric bikes compared to mopeds in the United States
sources.searcher_note: HTTP 403 on both tandfonline and sciencedirect; title only. Search snippet (not evidence) says it used NEISS 2019-2023 code 3215, 268,828 weighted cases, e-bikes 28.2% and mopeds 53.3%, e-bikes rising faster.

notes: No source found reporting the combined e-bike-plus-moped code 3215 series (21.8K to 87.6K, 4.0x) or the all-injuries-flat comparison. Published figures split e-bikes out of 3215 by narrative and drop mopeds (CPSC: 34,200 e-bike ED visits in 2023, ~10x since 2017). The e-bike-vs-moped paper covers the same code and window but could not be fetched. Post-cutoff coverage exists (USAFacts 2026-08-20, WRDW 2026-09-25) but cites e-bike-only numbers.
